## Overview With pipeline parallelism, a model whose stages use different attention backends fails at startup. `resolve_kv_cache_layout` asserts that every worker reports the same list of supported KV cache layouts, but PP stages hold different layers, so their lists can differ. This PR makes the engine core merge the worker lists with the same rule `get_supported_kv_cache_layouts` already uses for the backends of one worker. This addresses failure 1 ("PP2 on SM100") of #60791. Failures 2-5 in that issue are not touched here. ## Claims - `vllm serve` of a 10-layer MiniMax-M3-MXFP8 with `--pipeline-parallel-size 2` on B200 now starts, picks `LBHNC`, and answers requests. Before, it died in `_initialize_kv_caches` with `AssertionError: Workers disagree on supported KV cache layouts`. - When all workers report the same list (one GPU, TP only, PP with equal stages), the result is the same as before. - If no layout is supported by every worker, the existing `ValueError` is still raised. - New unit test `test_pipeline_stages_resolve_a_layout_every_stage_supports`. It fails on the old code with the bug's assertion. ## Validation Hardware: 2 x NVIDIA B200 (SM100, x86_64). The issue was reported on GB200 (aarch64), which has the same SM. Software: vLLM `0.31.1rc1.dev173+g8cbd5d030` (commit `8cbd5d03006c33185f402249ff2b448efd594986`), with and without this patch. Attention backend chosen: FLASHINFER. Model: the issue's 10-layer cut of `MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3-MXFP8` is not published, so I rebuilt it from the Hub checkpoint (revision `c5454eb03678d8710e54a4e0fc681b9f3b4a3dba`) with the script below. Layers 0-2 are dense and layers 3-9 are sparse. I cannot show it is tensor-identical to the reporter's cut.
cut script (replace $HF_HOME with your Hugging Face cache path) ```python # Cut MiniMax-M3-MXFP8 to its first 10 decoder layers (+ vision tower), as the report describes. import json, re, glob, os, shutil, sys from safetensors import safe_open from safetensors.torch import save_file src = glob.glob("$HF_HOME/hub/models--MiniMaxAI--MiniMax-M3-MXFP8/snapshots/*")[0] dst = "/tmp/m3-10layer" os.makedirs(dst, exist_ok=True) N = 10 for f in os.listdir(src): if f.endswith(".safetensors") or f == "model.safetensors.index.json": continue shutil.copy(os.path.realpath(os.path.join(src, f)), os.path.join(dst, f)) def trunc(o): if isinstance(o, dict): return {k: trunc(v) for k, v in o.items()} if isinstance(o, list) and len(o) == 60 and all(isinstance(x, int) for x in o): return o[:N] return o cfg = json.load(open(os.path.join(dst, "config.json"))) cfg["text_config"] = trunc(cfg["text_config"]); cfg["text_config"]["num_hidden_layers"] = N q = cfg["quantization_config"] q["ignored_layers"] = [x for x in q["ignored_layers"] if not (m := re.search(r"layers\.(\d+)\.", x)) or int(m.group(1)) < N] json.dump(cfg, open(os.path.join(dst, "config.json"), "w"), indent=2) wm = {} for shard in sorted(glob.glob(src + "/*.safetensors")): out = {} with safe_open(shard, "pt") as f: for k in f.keys(): m = re.search(r"language_model\.model\.layers\.(\d+)\.", k) if m and int(m.group(1)) >= N: continue out[k] = f.get_tensor(k) name = os.path.basename(shard) save_file(out, os.path.join(dst, name), metadata={"format": "pt"}) for k in out: wm[k] = name print(name, len(out), flush=True) json.dump({"metadata": {}, "weight_map": wm}, open(os.path.join(dst, "model.safetensors.index.json"), "w")) ```
Reproducer. It fails at startup, so no request is needed to see the bug: ```bash CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1 VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S=3600 \ vllm serve /tmp/m3-10layer --trust-remote-code --block-size 128 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \ --attention-config '{"indexer_kv_dtype":"fp8"}' \ --disable-hybrid-kv-cache-manager --enable-prefix-caching --pipeline-parallel-size 2 ``` Before: 4 of 4 runs failed like this, about 160 s after start. 3 runs used the `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-8cbd5d03006c33185f402249ff2b448efd594986` image and 1 used a source install. One more source run never got this far, because of a file permission problem in my setup, so it is not counted. ``` AssertionError: Workers disagree on supported KV cache layouts: [['LBHNC', 'BLHNC'], ['LBNHC', 'LBHNC', 'BLNHC', 'BLHNC', 'BHLNC', 'LHBNC']]. ``` After: 5 of 5 runs started and answered one request with HTTP 200. 3 of the runs used the final code (the last one was run by a separate reviewer) and 2 used an earlier version of the patch. ``` Using LBHNC KV cache layout. INFO: Application startup complete. "POST /v1/completions HTTP/1.1" 200 OK ``` The request was `curl -s localhost:8000/v1/completions -d '{"model":"/tmp/m3-10layer","prompt":"The capital of France is","max_tokens":8,"temperature":0}'`. The returned text is junk, which is expected from a 10-layer cut of a much deeper model. I did not run an accuracy eval. Startup takes more than 10 minutes, mostly for FlashInfer autotuning of the MXFP8 MoE kernels. Unit tests (run with `--noconftest`, because my environment had no `tblib`, which `tests/conftest.py` imports): - `pytest --noconftest tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py -k pipeline_stages`: passes with this patch. With the old `vllm/v1/attention/backends/utils.py` it fails with the same `Workers disagree on supported KV cache layouts` assertion. - `tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py`, `tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_attention_backends_selection.py`, `tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_kv_cache_layout.py`: 197 passed, 76 skipped. The 8 errors are tests that need the `caplog_vllm` fixture from `tests/conftest.py`. The 2 failures are PP tests that need 4 GPUs (`World size (4) is larger than the number of available GPUs (1)`). They fail the same way on the old code with 1 GPU, and they pass with 4 GPUs visible. - `pre-commit run --files` on both changed files: all hooks pass. ## Details Root cause: each worker reports the layouts that all of its own attention backends support (`WorkerBase.get_supported_kv_cache_layouts`). `resolve_kv_cache_layout` then asserted that all reports are equal, because "all ranks run the same backends". With PP, each stage builds only its own layers. For this model with PP2: - PP0 holds layers 0-4. Layers 0-2 use FlashInfer, which supports only `(LBHNC, BLHNC)` on SM100, so PP0 reports `['LBHNC', 'BLHNC']`. - PP1 holds layers 5-9, which are all sparse. `MINIMAX_M3_SPARSE` and `MINIMAX_M3_SPARSE_INDEXER` declare no layout set, so PP1 reports the default list of six layouts. The two lists differ, but they share `LBHNC` and `BLHNC`. With PP=1 the model works, because one worker sees all backends and intersects their sets. A debug run that printed each stage's backends confirmed this. Fix: the merge code in `get_supported_kv_cache_layouts` moves into a helper, `_merge_supported_layouts`, and `resolve_kv_cache_layout` now uses the helper on the worker reports. - Identical lists keep their order, so setups where all workers agree are unchanged. - Otherwise, the candidates are the layouts that appear in every list, and the layout that the most lists put first wins. - A worker that reports the default list (no backend declares a set) does not vote, in the same way that a backend that declares nothing does not vote inside one worker. Without this rule, an all-sparse stage would vote for `LBNHC`, and PP could pick a different layout from PP=1. The second case of the new test covers this. - If no layout is in every list, the code still raises `ValueError: No KV cache layout satisfies every supported set`. Tradeoff: the removed assertion also caught TP ranks of one stage that report different lists, for example after one rank picked a different backend by mistake. Those lists are now merged like PP stages. The chosen layout is still one that every worker supports. A per-stage check could be added back, but the engine core would then need to know which worker is in which stage, and this fix does not need that. Limitations: only failure 1 of the issue is fixed. Validation used B200 with FLASHINFER and `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1`, not GB200. ---

(Mandatory for agents, optional for humans). - [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR. - [ ] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity. - [ ] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI. - [ ] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples. - [ ] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.

+def test_pipeline_stages_resolve_a_layout_every_stage_supports(monkeypatch):
+    """PP stages hold different layers, so their workers can report different
+    supported layouts (e.g. only one stage has FlashInfer layers on SM100)."""
+    from vllm.v1.attention.backends.utils import (
+        get_supported_kv_cache_layouts,
+        resolve_kv_cache_layout,
+    )
+
+    monkeypatch.delenv("VLLM_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT", raising=False)
+    config = VllmConfig(model_config=ModelConfig(max_model_len=1024))
+    config.cache_config.kv_cache_layout = None
+    any_layout = [layout.name for layout in get_supported_kv_cache_layouts([])]
+    layout = resolve_kv_cache_layout(config, [["LBHNC", "BLHNC"], any_layout])
+    assert layout == KVCacheLayout.LBHNC
+
+    # A stage that declares nothing must not outvote a declared preference.
+    config.cache_config.kv_cache_layout = None
+    layout = resolve_kv_cache_layout(config, [["BLHNC", "LBNHC"], any_layout])
+    assert layout == KVCacheLayout.BLHNC
+
+    config.cache_config.kv_cache_layout = None
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="No KV cache layout satisfies"):
+        resolve_kv_cache_layout(config, [["LBHNC"], ["LBNHC"]])
+
